decided: If an earlier pull-request step of the same command failed, such as opening the pull request at propose or the final push at archive, the closing commit does nothing at all. The user is left with the recovery commands that failure printed, and they still work.
alternatives: let the closing commit run anyway and remove the record commit from the recovery commands propose prints
why: The rule for a failed step already says no later pull-request step runs, and the closing commit is one of those steps. Running it would commit the record, retry a push that just failed, and make the printed recovery fail.

relies_on.title: PR actions are workflow-body choreography (zero engine git)
